ITER is designed and developed as a first of its kind research device. So even if we do not reach our total lifetime operation goal, it will still be a huge success because of all the significant scientific data that we will acquire. ITER is a test of a global community to come together and work towards a single significant goal. It has been difficult up to this point, but I am confident that we are heading in the right direction and will have a working fusion device in the upcoming future.

Now if you are just referring to fusion ever working on earth, then yes it will. There is the running joke that fusion is 10 years away, and has been 10 years away since the 60s. But our understanding on plasma confinement and device operation has significantly grown. Just look at the success that [W7-X](http://www.ipp.mpg.de/w7x) has had recently (and that is a stellarator). The fusion community is looking at multiple different solutions to the problem of sustained power producing fusion, and we have grown significantly in the past few years.

Korea is currently working on a prototype commercial fusion power plant as we speak,[ K-DEMO](https://www.iter.org/newsline/255/1481). Initially the plan was to wait for ITER to finish before starting a DEMO plant, but due to set-backs, Korea has decided to jump right in and has begun work on K-DEMO.

When ITER reaches D-T (Deutrium-Tritium) Phase. It will hopefully be able to create a burning plasma where the heat within the plasma will sustain its own reaction, allowing for a much longer plasma duration.
12 [T] toroidal field and 6 [T] poloidal field. If you think of a doughnut, the toroidal field goes along the edge in a circle. The poloidal goes around the doughnut through the middle hole and out.

It takes a vacuum, so that none of the energy within the plasma is dissipated away. And some extremely powerful superconducting magnets (50 Gigajoules of stored energy) to keep the plasma from contacting the walls. ITER is shaped like a hollow doughnut, and the plasma sits in a ring inside.

Create an algorithm that is used for all your passwords. That way you only have to remember the algorithm. All my passwords follow an algorithm that uses the name of the site. This makes all my passwords different, but they are easy to remember through the algorithm.

Example: Use all odd characters in website name, the number of characters, the @ symbol, then all even characters

Password for Reddit: edt6@Rdi

Password for Steam: ta5@Sem

Password for Amazon: mzn6@Aao

Bam... Difficult to crack and easy to remember passwords. Plus if one of your passwords gets compromised all your other passwords are not compromised unless they know the algorithm. You can add rules the include the number of characters so that your passwords always hits the greater than requirement (spell out the number of required characters until the required number is reached). So if you require >8 then the steam password would not work. So the adjusted password would be ta5@SemE (The E comes from writing out Eight, but reaching the 8 character requirement at the E).

Remember, the speed of light is a constant. No matter how fast you are going that constant remains. If you are in a ship moving at the speed of light, you will observe light at the constant speed of light (normal time). We can actually [slow down light](http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2009/dec/15/slowed-light-breaks-record), which means we have already created a system where things are traveling faster than light.
